 Judgment

The claimants are in appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the Motor Accident Claims NC: 2023:KHC-K:1350 Tribunal No.IV, Vijayapur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.1965/2016, vide judgment and award dated 27.09.2019.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The claimants are the dependent legal heirs of deceased Siddamma, who died in a road accident,
when a bike bearing registration No.KL-10/AG-3583 (henceforth referred as 'offending vehicle')
dashed against her.
The claimants claimed that the deceased was 52 years old and was running a pan shop and was purportedly earning a sum of Rs.10,000/- per month.

They claimed that the deceased used to contribute her income for the upkeep of the family and hence, they filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

Mahananda And Ors vs Ashraf S/O Alavikutti And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84736541/
2 3.

entities.text: Mahananda And Ors vs Ashraf S/O Alavikutti And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The insurer contested the claim petition and admitted that the offending vehicle was duly insured with it, but the registered owner a person named, Ashraf S/o. Alavikutti.

It claimed that there was no privity of contract NC: 2023:KHC-K:1350 between it and respondent No.3 and therefore,
contended that it was not liable to indemnify the owner of the offending vehicle.
It also claimed that the deceased while crossing the road was negligent and hence contributed to the accident.
Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
4. Claimant No.2 was examined as P.W.1 and she marked Exs.P.1 to P.15.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.
5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending motorcycle.

It held that the deceased was aged 55 years and as there was no proof of income, the Tribunal considered her notional income at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and deducted 1/3rd towards her personal and living expenses and awarded the following compensation:
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1350 Sl.No. Heads Compensation 1. Loss of Rs.5,28,000/-
Dependency 2. Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
3. Loss of Love and Rs.40,000/-
Affection 4.

Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Total Rs.5,98,000/-
 6.

The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending motorcycle to pay the compensation along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation, the claimants are in appeal.

7. Learned counsel for the claimants submitted that the Tribunal committed an error in considering notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/-
per month, while in similar circumstances, this Court has considered the notional income of a person dying or injured in the accident in the year 2016 at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.

He Mahananda And Ors vs Ashraf S/O Alavikutti And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84736541/
3 further submitted that the Tribunal also failed to award future prospects in view of NC:
2023:KHC-K:1350 the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd.
Vs. Pranay Sethi1.

entities.text: He Mahananda And Ors vs Ashraf S/O Alavikutti And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, he prays that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal be enhanced.

8. Learned counsel for the insurer however contended that the deceased was 55 years old and the income at a sum of Rs.6,000/- taken by the Tribunal is just ant proper and therefore, submits that there is no scope for enhancement of compensation.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants as well as the learned counsel for the insurer.
I have also perused the records of the Tribunal and its judgment and award.
10. The accident and consequent death of the deceased in the accident is not in dispute.
The accident occurred in the year 2016.
This Court has consistently (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC-K:1350 taken notional income of the persons dying or injured in a road traffic accident in the year 2016 at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
Consequently, there is no reason why the said benefit should not be extended to the claimants.
The claimants were also entitled to loss of future prospects at 10% of the notional income of the deceased.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is determined as follows:
 Sl.No. Heads Amount  1. Loss of dependency Rs.8,47,044/-
 (Rs.8,750/- + Rs.875/-
 (10%)= Rs.9,625/- -
 rd  Rs.3,208/- (1/3 ) =
 Rs.6,417/- x 12 x 11 )
 2. Loss of parental Rs.44,000/-
 consortium to claimant
No.3 3

. Loss of estate, funeral Rs.33,000/-
expenses and incidental expenses Total Rs.9,24,044/-
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1350 11.
In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.5,98,000/- to Rs.9,24,044/-.
The enhanced compensation shall be paid by the insurer of the offending vehicle along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
